question: How does doubling the panel count change the absolute integration errors of trapezoid and left-endpoint sums for x² on [0,1]?
hypotheses: The composite trapezoid estimate exceeds 1/3 by 1/(6n²); doubling n gives observed order two.
Left-endpoint sums converge from below with order approaching one, not two.
protocol: Use n = 4, 8, 16, 32, 64 equal panels, in that order. Evaluate f(x) = x*x at mesh points and compute each weighted sum directly in Python, not from the error formula.
Use 1/3 as the reference. For each method record absolute error E(n); from the second row onward compute p(n) = log2(E(n/2)/E(n)). Leave the first order fields blank.

Compare trapezoid signed errors with the independently derived formula at every n. Compare observed orders with the declared intervals below; retain the left sums as a negative control on the same mesh.
Save CSV and plot the two absolute-error series on log scales. Reproduce both artifacts and the completion record byte-for-byte from a clean directory.

criteria.description: Derive the exact reference and signed trapezoid error. On every sampled mesh the signed difference estimate minus 1/3 must match 1/(6n²) within 1e-14 absolute.
All four trapezoid orders must be within 1e-9 of two.
Left estimates must stay below 1/3 and absolute errors must decrease. All four left orders must lie in [0.9, 1.1], excluding two.
